title.suggested: Joe Goss Arrives in America; Allen Challenges Coburn

summary.suggested: The St. Louis Globe-Democrat reported that Joe Goss, who fought Allen to a draw in 1867, had arrived in America, and that Allen offered to fight Joe Coburn, who billed himself champion boxer of America, for any stakes.

metadata.notes: Masthead: St. Louis Daily Globe-Democrat, Tuesday Morning, April 11, 1876, page 8.

facts.fact: Allen received a dispatch from Jem Coyne of Newark, N.J., announcing that Joe Goss had arrived in America
Allen and Joe Goss fought in a twenty-four-foot ring for £100 a side and the middleweight championship; after 34 rounds lasting 1 hour 52 minutes the fight was declared a draw
Allen played the crib scene from Tom and Jerry at the Theatre Comique, St. Louis, a couple of weeks before

Allen offered to fight Joe Coburn for as much money as he could raise or for nothing, at a point halfway between St. Louis and New York, or else a glove fight to a finish, betting $500 he would make Coburn take off the gloves
places: halfway between St. Louis and New York

notes: The Tom and Jerry fact matches an existing fact listed with id 000 ('performs Tom and Jerry on stage'), so existing_fact is left blank. The paper says Allen had fought nine times since 1867.
